notes.title: Version 1.0.5
notes.notes:
This is a major balance patch which adds a lot of possible solutions for conclusions and interruptions, making the game less strict and more open to different ways of thinking. We also added a new difficulty mode in between the easy and hard difficulty for a more balanced experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42791427/618c0b535e1eec0b17cca17f47f0c198662ce67d.png[/img]

Dear prosecutors,

After watching a lot of you play and make reviews and community posts regarding the game’s difficulty, we’ve carefully taken notes and created a major balancing patch. The game is a lot less strict about what it considers the correct solution now as we’ve added many alternative combinations for conclusions as well as many more alternative correct solutions for interruptions during witness interviews. Many of the steps can be solved with more ways of thinking than we realized initially, and this patch addresses this.
Furthermore, after watching people struggle with the difficulty selection between only an easy-mode and a hard mode, we’ve now added a normal difficulty mode in between. The new mode in the middle no longer requires you to select individual paragraphs. This should hopefully make the game more approachable for those who want a bit of a challenge without wanting to choose the highest possible difficulty.
We hope that you’ll enjoy this new update and are looking forward to reading your feedback about the new difficulty mode and newly accepted solutions.

As with all updates, it can happen that new bugs are introduced, even though we thoroughly tested every newly added solution. So, if you encounter any bugs while playing, we’d be very grateful if you could report them by pressing F5 while in game.

See you in court!
Your Paintbucket team.

[h2]Difficulty & Balance[/h2]
[list]
[*]Adjusted the difficulty of Investigator Mode to make it a little easier. (Removed the requirement to specify the paragraph in a given document, and enabled the counter in the testimonies that shows how many optional interactables have been found). 
From the feedback we received, we feel that this more closely reflects the kind of "normal" difficulty that people are looking for - whereas in our minds, "Investigator Mode" was always designed to be "Hard Mode".
[*]Added a new difficulty setting, "Prosecutor Mode", which is the former Investigator Mode aka "Hard Mode".
[*]Added a lot more documents & paragraphs as possible solutions for interruptions and conclusions.
[*]Removed Esther's misleading comments when combining documents into conclusions.
[/list]
[h2]Graphics[/h2]
[list]
[*]Changed the used Anti-aliasing method(s) from MSAA + SMAA (Medium) to just SMAA (Quality), resulting in a sharper image and higher framerates on certain systems.
[/list]
[h2]Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*]Fixed an issue where the interruption UI would display its animations abnormally.
[*]Fixed Theresa being called Edwina in the court opening cutscene of the second case.
[*]Fixed a bug which can lead to players being stuck when entering a coworkers office.
[*]Fixed various typos and grammatical errors in all languages in the game.
[/list]

notes.title: Behind The Scenes & SteamDeck Update
notes.notes:
I'll be honest, the night before our Kickstarter launched, I barely slept. Going public with our niche game, we wondered if anyone would notice - well they ... you! ... did. 

A huge thank you for your support, kind words, and feedback, it really means the world to us! 🧡

Today, I would like to share a peek behind the scenes of developing The Darkest Files for the last two years and show you how we got here.

[b]Welcome to the Chronicles of Crime - Today: Starting a Case![/b]

It all starts with research. The cases in The Darkest Files are based on real crimes of the time. This means going through archives, files, newspapers, and literature on possible cases to a) pick one that works with our game mechanics - not all cases do - and b) make sure that once we pick it, we get the facts right. While we do sometimes change characters or events for the game, we want to make sure that we know when we are doing so.

While working on The Darkest Files, we went through dozens of potential cases to pick the ones that would work for us. We would have liked to do more, but to quote your in-game co-prosecutor, Mr Peters: "There are so many of them and so few of us."

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42791427/a4b03ce78a9f3fee8a85281ab898dd18cc0666c7.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42791427/f30eb5162ebfb4e7990c9441fbba02553ec4b384.png[/img]
Historical inspiration and an early draft of the reconstruction board that you will be using in the game to draft your theory of the crime and how it ended up looking in the game

After researching a historical case, the game designers arrange the events to make them playable: they decide which witness unveils which clue, what files need to be found and how, and who sends the investigators off course.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42791427/0338d6f6e65ef1b2208d134c14ef42f255f983a6.png[/img]

A storyboard artist and designer takes over and creates storyboards and mock-ups of key scenes helping us to better imagine how things will feel in the game.

From bio and description, the character artists create the NPC, skeleton, and poses. So many poses!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42791427/d05c0425389f0f0f001431800fefcaba67e28574.jpg[/img]

Just as for characters and scenes, the 2D artists draw sketches of the environments. The 3D artists model the environments creating walkable, interactive spaces. 
Once built, our brilliant technical artist uses her shader wizardry to turn everything into an explorable graphic novel. And here you go: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42791427/b99f1a7a7a5787faece5a116c5bf44fa1e2d436b.png[/img]

You can play The Darkest Files on your Steam Deck and enjoy the full experience! Sitting on the couch while investigating case files, interrogating witnesses at your own pace, or just relaxing on the bed while you review evidence and build your case. Bring Fritz Bauer's quest for justice with you wherever you go and experience this powerful historical story in a comfortable setting. Check it out on your Steam Deck today!

notes.title: The Darkest Files - Blueprint Board
notes.notes:
Solving crimes is not an easy task. That's where the Blueprint Board comes in handy! It's your tool to reconstruct the crime, connect the dots, and uncover the truth in “The Darkest Files”. 🕵️

Here's how it works: With the information you gathered through interviews with witnesses and by searching through documents, you step into the shoes of an investigator. On the Blueprint Board, you'll find the floor plan of the crime scene and solve the puzzle.

As you follow a timeline, you can place witnesses or suspects exactly where they were at crucial moments. You'll assign actions to them, determining who gave the orders or who pulled the trigger. You can even compare statements from the suspects on the board. This allows you to gain insight into who may be lying and who is telling the truth! With the Blueprint Board you will build your theory, the foundation for defending the case in court. ⚖️

notes.title: The Darkest Files - Behind the Scenes III
notes.notes:
One of the most significant challenges in developing an investigation game is striking the perfect balance in difficulty. Some players crave a tough, mind-bending challenge to solve the case, while others prefer a smooth experience, focusing on the story without getting stuck on an insurmountable obstacle.
To address this, we've introduced multiple difficulty levels and the option to customize individual settings, allowing players to tailor the challenge to their preferences. Does time pressure ruin the fun for you? Adjust the challenge timers or disable them completely. Are you a completionist who needs to find every hidden clue? Enable a display that reveals the number of clues discovered and those remaining.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42791427/c20f5662c4f1b26167df1775ccebb0743d748c4b.png[/img]

For players who want to immerse themselves in the story, the game eases the investigative process by providing certain evidence automatically and limiting the options in the interruption challenge to just three documents. Those who tried the demo have experienced this approach.
Conversely, if you seek a more challenging investigation, be prepared to work hard to uncover evidence. In the interruption challenge, you won't receive any pre-selection, meaning you'll need to identify the correct document from all available options. Additionally, you must pinpoint the relevant section within the document to successfully overcome the challenge. Our newly implemented text marking feature comes in handy here. And, if desired, you can also experience all this under time pressure. Players familiar with the demo will be pleasantly surprised by the increased difficulty in solving a case.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42791427/b31430bb612711816bfa43b88887986152fd4a8e.png[/img]

Overall, our diverse difficulty settings should be able to cater to a range of playstyles, ensuring an enjoyable and immersive experience for all true crime enthusiasts.
What do you think about this approach? Are you more interested in experiencing the story or are you looking for a challenge in detective games?

Let's start with the main cast of the Insurgent case. There were originally a lot more characters planned for this case, but we ended up scrapping them. Not only because it became too much for us developers, but also for the players. When we created the cast of characters, we made sure that they were not only different in appearance, but also in body type. We wanted players to be able to tell them apart as much as possible, even if they were wearing the same uniform. During development, we made a few adjustments here and there. For example, Hermann Kiebitz is now significantly smaller and wears glasses.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42791427/62f3e2db15bc03f8aa3fbdc2d8da7082d88d7c09.png[/img]

Esther Katz has two collegues: Christoph Wollmuth and Simon Peters. While Christoph seems quite relaxed, Simon is rather neat and uptight. This difference in their personalities is something we wanted to show in their character designs as well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42791427/2954aa69bd1ce3d9627c90d5a5f026fe8d6eb3ad.png[/img]
